clue.text: Suits, best if tailor-made

indicators.note: something tailor-made is cut and stitched to a new shape, so the letters of the two words are refashioned

explanation.surface: An advert for suits made to measure, which look best that way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailor-made' looks like it describes the suits, but it rearranges BESTIF into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To suit someone is to be fitting or proper for them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Man on board is bound to follow bosun's lead

indicators.note: says the pieces after it come behind the bosun's letter in the answer
a word's lead is its leading letter, so only the opening of the sailor's title is used

parts.note: taken as written
a bound is a leap, as is a hop

explanation.surface: A sailor must obey the boatswain's orders on deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board' suggests a ship's deck, beside the bosun; it is a chessboard, where a bishop is one of the pieces ('men').
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop is one of the chess pieces, which are traditionally called men, on a chessboard.

clue.text: Self-employed worker erected shelter in the country

indicators.note: one piece is set inside the name of the nation

parts.note: France, the country across the Channel

indicators.note: in a down clue, something erected is stood upright, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: A self-employed person put up a shelter somewhere in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erected' only works in a down clue: the shelter word is read upward, giving EEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A freelance sells their work to various clients instead of being on one employer's payroll.

clue.text: Tax cut Conservative introduced, small one

indicators.note: the party initial is put into the middle of the shortened tax
a word that is cut is docked, here losing its final letter

parts.note: a tithe was a tax of a tenth paid to the church

explanation.surface: A political report: a Tory government brought in a small tax cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks the tax's last letter. Titch is British slang for a small person, often a nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Titch is informal British slang for a very small person, often a nickname.

clue.text: Report of shop recently opened in foreign city

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the phrase is the spoken form of the words

parts.note: a delicatessen just opened is a new deli

explanation.surface: News of a shop that has just opened in a city abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'new deli' matches the Indian capital, NEW DELHI.
explanation.definitionFit: New Delhi, the capital of India, is a city abroad from a British viewpoint.

clue.text: Betraying no emotion, so lost for words?

definitions.meaning: showing nothing on the face, blank
read cryptically: having no expressions, that is no phrases or words to say

explanation.definitionFit: An expressionless face shows no feeling; read literally, the word also means lacking any spoken expressions.

clue.text: Rebel isn't stopping faction supporting Democrat

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below, so the Democrat letter comes on top
the faction is plugged into the contraction like a stopper

parts.note: the contraction written out without its apostrophe
a side is a faction or party in a dispute

explanation.surface: A rebel refuses to stop backing a party that supports a Democrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stopping' plugs the faction into the contraction, giving ISSIDENT; in a down clue 'supporting' puts D on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissident is someone who opposes official policy, a rebel against the authorities.

clue.text: End of motorway with lights on either side

indicators.note: the word for lights is split so its parts flank the road on each side

parts.note: lit means lights, as in lights a fire
M1, Britain's first motorway, is written MI in crosswords

explanation.surface: The end of a motorway, lined with lamps on both sides.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's London to Leeds motorway; crosswords read the digit 1 as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A limit is a boundary or furthest point, where something ends.

clue.text: One has high hopes having sorted contents of suggestions box?

definitions.meaning: a person with lofty, perhaps unrealistic aims
the suggestions in such a box sorted into a list would be a list of ideas

explanation.definitionFit: An idealist pursues high or perfect ideals, and split in two the word is a list of ideas.

clue.text: Cold tart with crisp base — see us tucking in for dessert

indicators.note: in a down clue the base is the bottom, so this piece comes last

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
tart is slang for a promiscuous woman, as is harlot

indicators.note: the pronoun is tucked into the word for crisp

parts.note: terse speech is crisp and brief
taken as written

explanation.surface: A menu note: a cold tart with a crunchy base is served as pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking in' gives TERUSSE, placed at the base. A charlotte russe is a cold dessert of sponge fingers around a cream filling.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte russe is a classic cold pudding of Bavarian cream set inside a ring of sponge fingers.

clue.text: Workforce ultimately joins in strikes against hard work … here?

definitions.text: Workforce ultimately joins in strikes against hard work … here?

indicators.note: against means next to, so the following pieces are placed beside it
the letter enters the word for strikes, joining in among its letters

parts.note: swats are sharp blows or strikes

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letter of the word is taken

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
op, short for opus, is a work of music

explanation.surface: Workers go on strike against hard labour, and this is the kind of place they would.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strikes' looks like industrial action, but it is SWATS, taking E to make SWEATS. The whole clue describes a sweatshop, where the staff might strike against hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweatshop is a workplace where people toil long hours in poor conditions for low pay.

clue.text: Map of sorts led back to French woman's address in Picardy area

indicators.note: led back means taken in the opposite direction, so the letters read right to left

parts.note: OS stands for Ordnance Survey, the British mapmakers, so a kind of map
Mme, short for Madame, is how a French woman is addressed

explanation.surface: A map of some kind leads back to the address of a French woman in Picardy.
explanation.walkthrough: Ordnance Survey is Britain's national mapping agency; 'led back' gives SO. Picardy is a region of northern France.
explanation.definitionFit: The Somme is a department and river in Picardy, northern France, famous for the 1916 battle.

clue.text: Bird diving into shallow lake

indicators.note: the answer dives into the two words, sitting inside them across the gap

explanation.surface: A bird plunges into a shallow lake.
explanation.definitionFit: An owl is a nocturnal bird of prey, a straightforward example of a bird.

clue.text: Firearm such as Colt?

parts.note: Colt is a famous gun maker, but a colt is also a young horse, so the gun is pictured as horse-related

explanation.definitionFit: A horse pistol was a large pistol carried by a rider on horseback, in a holster at the saddle.

clue.text: Footballer's nifty play results in win for away team, apparently

definitions.meaning: a quick pass and return between two players to beat a defender, a wall pass
a final score of one goal to the home side and two to the visitors looks like a phrase of two numbers

explanation.definitionFit: A one-two is a quick give-and-go pass in football; a 1-2 scoreline also means the away side won.

clue.text: Composition of Elgar isn't for percussion instruments

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so the letters are arranged anew

explanation.surface: A piece by Elgar that is not written for drums and other percussion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composition' suggests music by Elgar, but it rearranges ELGARISNT.
explanation.definitionFit: Triangles are struck metal percussion instruments in an orchestra, so these are examples.

clue.text: Variety of plants found round city area

indicators.note: the word for plants goes round the city letters, enclosing them

parts.note: plants are undercover agents, or spies
EC, East Central, is the postcode area of the City of London

explanation.surface: A kind of plant found growing around an urban district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plants' reads as greenery, but means SPIES, as in planted agents. EC is the City of London's postcode district.
explanation.definitionFit: A species is a kind or sort, a classification of living things of one variety.

clue.text: Accepted money I've offered as extra payment

parts.note: in means accepted or fashionable
a cent is a small coin, money
the contraction written out without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone accepts the cash offered as a bonus.
explanation.definitionFit: An incentive is a bonus or inducement paid to encourage effort, an extra payment.

clue.text: Delayed departure, say, having extra burden to carry

indicators.note: say signals that the words are spoken, so the sound is what counts

parts.note: to delay leaving is to have waited

explanation.surface: Someone delayed leaving because of the heavy load they had to carry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delayed departure' gives WAITED, which spoken matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Weighted means loaded down or burdened, given extra weight to bear.

clue.text: English stickler for the law loses heart to poet

indicators.note: the word loses its central letters, its heart

parts.note: a legalist insists on the strict letter of the law

explanation.surface: An English pedant over legal rules loses courage when faced with a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses heart' drops AL from the middle of LEGALIST, leaving LEGIST.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegist writes elegies, mournful poems, so is a kind of poet.

clue.text: Ill-educated type concealing books not yet paid for

indicators.note: the type hides the books within his own letters

parts.note: an oick is British slang for a coarse, uneducated lout, also spelt oik
NT is the New Testament, books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A badly educated man hides the books he has not paid for.
explanation.walkthrough: OICK is a variant spelling of OIK, British slang for a lout. 'On tick' is British for on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Bought on tick means bought on credit, so not yet paid for.

clue.text: Gay set, terribly camp

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly done, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A group of gay men behaving in an awfully camp way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges GAYSET.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagey and camp both mean theatrically exaggerated or affected in manner.

clue.text: Gross French individual in Lourdes violated basic principles

parts.note: GR is the abbreviation for gross, twelve dozen

indicators.note: the French word is set inside the scrambled town name
violated means broken, so the letters of the town are rearranged

parts.note: un is French for one, a single individual

explanation.surface: A gross Frenchman in Lourdes broke the most basic rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'violated' rearranges the town into ODRULES, and 'in' puts the French word after its O.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground rules are the basic principles agreed for how something will be conducted.

clue.text: Due to time being wasted, move quickly

indicators.note: the time letter is squandered and lost, so it is removed from the little word

parts.note: to wing is to fly or travel swiftly

explanation.surface: Because time has been wasted, someone needs to hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Due to' looks like a phrase, but 'Due' is the definition; 'to' loses its T to leave O.
explanation.definitionFit: Owing means due, as money owing is still to be paid.

clue.text: Run down list of candidates

definitions.meaning: a set of nominees put forward for election

explanation.definitionFit: To slate is to criticise severely, and a slate is also a list of candidates in an election.

clue.text: Head teachers

definitions.meaning: the ..., the National Union of Teachers, was a British teaching union

explanation.definitionFit: Nut is slang for the head, and the NUT was the National Union of Teachers in Britain.

clue.text: After short drive a learner's given test

indicators.note: the following pieces come after the shortened outing
short means docked of its final letter

parts.note: a drive is an outing or trip
L is the learner plate letter on British cars

explanation.surface: After a brief spin, a learner driver is given their driving test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' leaves TRI. L plates mark a learner driver in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial is a test of performance or quality, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Saw round tree, making casual progress

indicators.note: the proverb goes round the tree, enclosing it

parts.note: a saw is an old saying or proverb
the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: Someone saws round a tree, making leisurely headway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a tool or a verb, but it is an old proverb; the tree sits after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sashaying is walking in a casual, swaggering way, so moving along easily.

clue.text: Understood synopsis supplied to editor

parts.note: a digest is a summary or synopsis

explanation.surface: Someone grasped the summary given to the editor.
explanation.definitionFit: To have digested information is to have absorbed and understood it.

clue.text: Tall thin male's swallowed medicine

indicators.note: the word for tall and thin has taken the male letter down inside it

parts.note: reedy means tall and thin, like a reed

explanation.surface: A lanky man has swallowed his medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'male's swallowed' means the male has been swallowed: M goes inside REEDY.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy is a medicine or treatment that cures a disease.
